response.markdown_report:
**Proposal: frequency-matched lexical stress testing for one frozen NextItNet per category.** At 10% research progress, prioritize an inexpensive diagnostic extension before changing the backbone or training objective.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, Electronics has a 12.96% sampled negative-win rate in the latest supplied diagnosis. This motivates closer candidate analysis but does not establish validation weakness. Second, recent-history ablation changes margins more than older-history ablation across all categories. This demonstrates intervention sensitivity without identifying current intent. Third, the existing candidate audit already separates uniform, popularity, prefix-lexical and target-oracle competitors. Matching popularity across lexical conditions would help distinguish lexical difficulty from frequency effects.

**Insights from related work.** First, sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with catalog metrics [1]. Exact bounded catalog scoring therefore provides a useful diagnostic reference. Second, NextItNet uses causal dilated residual convolutions [2]. Its existing representations and scoring hooks permit frozen-model comparisons without fitting another predictor. Third, attribution approximations can miss intervention effects [3]. Direct paired score comparisons are a simpler initial experiment than gradient attribution.

These observations suggest three directions: candidate-distribution controls, component sensitivity, and evidence-aware interpretation. The common framework crosses **intervention site**—candidates, activations or evidence—with **outcome**—rank sensitivity, numerical response or annotation support. The principal gap is separating candidate similarity from popularity while avoiding claims about unobserved compatibility or preferences.

| Atomic idea | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency-matched lexical audit [1] | 4: useful controlled combination / established matching | 7: sharpens sampling diagnosis / training memorization remains | 4: reuses retrieval / sparse strata complicate matching |
| Small residual-branch scaling [2,3] | 4: family-specific adaptation / established intervention | 6: locates sensitivity / no guaranteed accuracy gain | 5: bounded inference / hook and restoration care |
| Evidence-supported usefulness rubric | 3: concrete operational criteria / familiar annotation approach | 6: separates unknown from mismatch / requires independent judgments | 5: simple schema / labeling effort |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze training prefixes and targets before scoring. Construct two sets of 99 unique eligible competitors: prefix-lexical candidates and random controls with identical counts in training-frequency bins. Exclude padding, prefix items and the target identically; retain other later positives and report their overlap. Report matching failures explicitly rather than silently replacing candidates.

Score both conditions using the same final nonpadding NextItNet feature. Aggregate paired rank and diagnostic hit@10 differences within user, then across users. On a prespecified bounded subset, count catalog outrankers exactly; compare independent uniform draws with the hypergeometric sampling law [1]. Weighted and lexical conditions receive no uniform-law calibration.

Retain `DiagnosisProbe`, its return schema, the interpreter and ModelView interfaces. Record supports, matching coverage, missing text, tie conventions and seeds. These training diagnostics establish candidate sensitivity; only the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 selects improvements. Preserve one checkpoint per category and all host training constraints.

idea.description: Extend the existing frozen NextItNet candidate audit with frequency-matched prefix-lexical competitors and random controls, plus bounded exact-catalog calibration of uniform sampling.
idea.motivation: The current audit changes lexical similarity and frequency together. Matching observed training frequency offers a more interpretable comparison of candidate difficulty, while exact catalog ranks expose the limits of sampled diagnostic success. Neither comparison establishes user intent or validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), metrics and metric_definitions, and every host ModelView interface. Build examples from permitted training histories with stable user IDs; never manufacture user IDs from loader rows. Freeze example manifests, frequency bins and candidate sets before neural scoring. Compute item counts from training interactions only and disclose that these counts may include events later than an audited prefix; this is a retrospective training diagnostic. Use only titles/descriptions for lexical retrieval. Exclude padding, prefix items and the target from both competitor conditions, and sample without replacement. Match competitor counts exactly within predefined frequency bins; report infeasible pairs, matching coverage and missing-text support. Do not silently broaden bins after inspecting results. Later training interactions are overlap annotations, not verified negative labels. Rank using an explicit deterministic tie order; count catalog outrankers under that same order. For N eligible competitors and K outrankers, uniform unique sampling gives X~Hypergeometric(N,K,99), with sampled hit@10 probability P(X<=9), when N>=99. This is conditional on the diagnostic pool and tie order, not a reconstruction of the host evaluator. Bound catalog scoring to 40 prespecified examples/category and chunk candidates. Aggregate repeated draws within prefix, prefixes within user, and bootstrap users only when stable IDs exist; distinguish draw variability from user resampling uncertainty. Use local RNG seed 42 and restore module modes and global RNG state. Preserve one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category with no score fusion. No inference architecture change is required, so retain the corrected predictor writer. Preserve all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, single-GPU execution and the shared budget. Report deployment parity unavailable unless actually checked. Model selection remains the host's pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        with preserve_rng_and_module_modes(self.view.model):
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_diagnostics(train_loader)
                examples = freeze_training_prefix_manifest(self.view.user_train)
                bins = predefined_frequency_bins(training_interaction_counts())
                for example in examples:
                    eligible = catalog_without_padding_prefix_and_target(example)
                    lexical = retrieve_prefix_lexical_candidates(example, eligible, k=99)
                    control = sample_unique_frequency_matched_control(
                        eligible, histogram(lexical, bins), local_seed=42)
                    if not exact_match_available(lexical, control):
                        record_matching_failure_and_support(example)
                        continue
                    sequence = left_pad(example.prefix)
                    t = largest_index_where_nonzero(sequence)
                    feature = self.view.log2feats(sequence)[t]
                    record_paired_diagnostic_ranks(
                        self.view.predict_score, feature, example.target,
                        lexical, control, fixed_tie_order=True)
                    record_later_training_positive_overlap(example, lexical, control)
                    if example in prespecified_catalog_subset:
                        N, K = count_catalog_outrankers_in_chunks(feature, example, eligible)
                        record_uniform_prediction(hypergeom_cdf(9, N, K, 99))
                        record_repeated_unique_uniform_draws(feature, example, eligible)
                metrics.update(aggregate_prefixes_then_users_with_support())
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt(raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
                        require_support_and_missingness=True,
                        distinguish_training_diagnostics_from_validation=True,
                        forbid_intent_or_compatibility_inference=True)

originality.positive: Adds a focused frequency control to the existing lexical stress audit and connects it to exact finite-population calibration.
originality.negative: Matching, lexical retrieval and hypergeometric calibration are established techniques; novelty lies in their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Could guide a subsequent single-model sampling intervention by identifying difficulty beyond coarse frequency differences.
future_potential.negative: Training memorization, lexical ambiguity and residual differences within frequency bins limit interpretation; no validation gain is demonstrated.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing frozen audit, metadata index and scoring interfaces without changing training or deployment architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact matching, pool definitions, tie handling, missing-text accounting and user-level aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes limitations and inconsistency of sampled recommendation metrics relative to their full-catalog counterparts.
Motivates separate reporting of sampled diagnostic results and bounded exact catalog ranks.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical stress tests measure preference quality.
Uniform finite-population calibration does not apply directly to weighted or lexical sampling.

related_work.title: Next Item Recommendation with Self-Attention? No: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Recommendation
contributions: Introduces NextItNet's causal dilated convolutional approach to sequential recommendation.
Provides the preserved backbone family for frozen feature and candidate-score comparisons.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed frequency-matched diagnostic.
Architectural receptive fields alone do not establish learned temporal importance.

related_work.title: AtP*: An Efficient and Scalable Method for Localizing LLM Behaviour to Components
contributions: Investigates gradient approximations to activation patching and their false negatives.
Supports directly checking intervention effects before interpreting weak attribution.
limitations: Evidence concerns language models rather than NextItNet.
Component attribution does not establish improved recommendation accuracy.
